sections.what: Checks the F1 source is refused without prototype permission, and that football and cricket are accepted.
sections.why: Likely reason: the F1 source is restricted, so it must be blocked by default.
sections.watch_out: Changing the rights flag in either the test or the adapter could allow a restricted source without warning.

summary: Unit tests for the three data adapters that turn recorded source files into events for cricket, Formula 1 and football.
purpose: Checks each adapter reads its recorded sample correctly, keeps facts exact, and respects data rights rules.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The comments say tests use recorded files only and no network.
how: Loads recorded sample files at the start. Checks every sport has an adapter or a source-pending entry. Checks the cricket sample has over 200 ball records. Checks F1 Bahrain 2023 gives one record per completed lap, keeps missing times empty, and orders records by time. Checks the football match gives 20 shots, 5 goals, and a score that matches the match record. Checks every output passes the incident schema. Checks the F1 source is refused unless prototype data is allowed.
inputs: Recorded sample files in the data fixtures folder.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: Expected numbers come from the sample files, so replacing a sample changes them. The rights check depends on the flag being passed correctly.
debug: If a count is off, check the matching fixture file. If the rights test fails, check the prototype flag handling in the F1 adapter.
